coherence.source_text: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques presents a timely opportunity to address longstanding challenges in Vietnamese secondary education, particularly within the Flipped Classroom model. Vietnamese students in grades 6–12 frequently struggle with self-directed pre-class preparation, lacking access to on-demand, pedagogically appropriate guidance when encountering difficulties during independent study. Simultaneously, existing AI tutoring tools are either financially inaccessible to Vietnamese institutions or fail to account for the linguistic and curricular specifics of the Vietnamese educational context.

coherence.source_text: This research investigates the application of parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques—primarily Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and Quantized LoRA (QLoRA)—to adapt open-source Large Language Models (LLaMA 3, Mistral, Qwen) for Vietnamese secondary and high school tutoring. The study constructs and curates a Vietnamese K-12 educational conversation dataset of approximately 746 curated samples, systematically investigating the relationship between data quality characteristics and fine-tuned model behavior. A comparative evaluation framework assessing both technical language quality metrics (perplexity, BERTScore) and pedagogical appropriateness dimensions (guided inquiry, scaffolding, Socratic questioning) is applied across baseline and fine-tuned model variants.

The research further delivers a functional web-based learning support system integrating the fine-tuned model, accessible to students during independent study phases of flipped classroom instruction.

The findings have direct implications for educational equity, flipped classroom implementation, and the broader development of educational AI in low-resource language contexts.
